what_it_does: Solving hard optimization puzzles (like the maximum cut problem) using annealing—gradually cooling a system to escape local traps—requires computing energy values repeatedly, an expensive O(n²) calculation where n is the problem size. This paper describes a device-algorithm co-design using ferroelectric transistors (transistors whose conductance can be changed and held by an electric field) arranged in a crossbar array to perform in-situ annealing directly in the memory. By computing energy changes incrementally (O(n) instead of O(n²)) and approximating the exponential cooling schedule with simpler fractional calculations implementable in hardware, the system can tackle Max-Cut problems with thousands of variables much faster than traditional annealers.
